questions.stem: A program looks like a legitimate utility, but once run it secretly opens a back door for an attacker. Which malware type is this?
questions.explanation: A Trojan is malware disguised as a legitimate program; running it secretly opens a back door for the attacker.
questions.trap: Ransomware encrypts files for extortion; it does not masquerade as a useful tool to open a back door.

questions.stem: Which malware burrows deep into the core of the operating system, hiding its presence from antivirus and even Task Manager?
questions.explanation: A rootkit embeds itself in the core of the OS and hides from antivirus and Task Manager, making it very hard to find.
questions.trap: A keylogger records keystrokes but does not necessarily hide itself in the OS core the way a rootkit does.

questions.stem: A user's CPU is pinned at 100% and the electricity bill spikes; investigation shows software using the machine to mine cryptocurrency for an attacker. Which malware is this?
questions.explanation: A cryptominer secretly steals CPU cycles to mine cryptocurrency for an attacker.
questions.trap: Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment; it does not quietly mine using your CPU.

questions.stem: Which malware runs entirely in system memory, never writing a file to disk, making it invisible to traditional file scanners?
questions.explanation: Fileless malware runs entirely in memory and never writes a file to disk, evading traditional signature-based file scanners.
questions.trap: A boot sector virus does write to the disk's boot area; the 'no file on disk' clue points to fileless.

questions.stem: What is the only method described as 100% guaranteed to remove malware from a system?

choices.text: Run a single antivirus scan in normal mode
Delete the suspicious file from the Downloads folder
A full OS reinstallation, ideally from a known-good image

questions.explanation: The only way to be 100% sure malware is gone is a full OS reinstallation, ideally from a known-good image.
questions.trap: A single AV scan can miss rootkits and fileless threats; it is not a guarantee of complete removal.

questions.stem: Which detection approach uses behavioral analysis ON A SINGLE DEVICE to detect threats and can automatically isolate that endpoint?
questions.explanation: EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) uses behavioral analysis on a single device and can automatically isolate it.
questions.trap: XDR correlates across endpoints, network, and cloud - it is the big-picture version, not the single-device one.

questions.stem: A company hires a third-party firm to run and manage their EDR for them. What is this service called?
questions.explanation: MDR (Managed Detection and Response) is when you hire a third-party company to manage your EDR for you.
questions.trap: XDR is a broader detection scope (endpoint+network+cloud), not the 'someone else manages it' service model.

questions.stem: Which detection model correlates data from endpoints, the network, AND the cloud to spot widespread attacks?
questions.explanation: XDR (Extended Detection and Response) is the big picture - it correlates endpoint, network, and cloud data to catch widespread attacks.
questions.trap: EDR watches a single endpoint; XDR is the city-wide surveillance that ties multiple sources together.

questions.stem: If Windows is too corrupted to boot, which environment gives you a command prompt BEFORE Windows loads to troubleshoot and repair?
questions.explanation: The Windows Recovery Environment lets you access a command prompt before Windows loads, to troubleshoot and repair the system.
questions.trap: Task Manager and Resource Monitor only run after Windows has loaded, so they can't help when the OS won't boot.

questions.stem: What is described as the BEST defense against social-engineering threats like phishing?

choices.text: Consistent user education and anti-phishing training

questions.explanation: The weakest link is often the human, so consistent user education and anti-phishing training is the best defense.
questions.trap: Hardware and file systems do nothing against social engineering, which targets people, not machines.
